fix.summary: Sustain the sole Spec finding as an Apply defect, but narrow its proposed comparison: resolutionScope must bound the tree paths changed by conflict resolution relative to the assigned merge's automatic merge result, not every path changed relative to the first parent. Direct test-first Fixer apply is authorized for exactly the class below.

classes.name: Issue22MergerResolutionScopeAtCompletion
classes.owner: Package-owned Merger Git-state and completed-output verification seam
classes.boundary: The active/completed state contract and production adapter in src/merger-git-state.ts, completed acceptance in src/merger-role.ts, the corresponding exported dependency surface only as required, direct Merger Git/runtime regressions, and the README completion claim. Do not change the Merger Soul or input/output profession, and do not add merge initiation, queue, publication, routing, generic Git policy, shell classification, or caller orchestration.
classes.disposition: Accepted with corrected Git semantics. At activation, the seam must establish and freeze the automatic merge-result tree for the exact admitted target/source and in-progress merge (the actual AUTO_MERGE tree where available, or an equivalently exact package-owned snapshot); failure to establish it safely aborts rather than yielding a role outcome. At completed verification, compare that frozen tree to the submitted merge commit's tree, with rename detection disabled and NUL-safe exact path handling so content, mode, addition, and deletion deltas produce their actual tree paths. Every such resolution-changed path must be in the immutable resolutionScope; an out-of-scope path aborts completion. Do not use targetObjectId..mergeCommitId or mergeCommitId^1..mergeCommitId as the scope oracle: those include clean source-side changes that belong to the authorized two-parent merge. Red: source adds source-only.txt, target/source conflict on conflict.txt, scope is only conflict.txt, and Merger also edits tracked unrelated.txt; current code accepts the clean exact-parent commit, while the automatic-tree-to-commit delta is {conflict.txt, unrelated.txt} and must reject unrelated.txt. Green companion: the same merge with only conflict.txt resolved must pass even though first-parent-to-commit also lists out-of-scope source-only.txt. Also prove that tampering with a clean source-side path outside scope is rejected because it differs from the frozen automatic result.

details.note:
Adjudicated at current HEAD 1de12c8bb426257e2b456f9df38048313813aaca. Post-review changes are docket-only; the Merger implementation is unchanged from fa794e7. Authority explicitly binds permitted resolution scope and permits Merger to edit/stage only the assigned resolution, so prompt-only delivery is insufficient under Apply burden. Current src/merger-git-state.ts returns only commit identity, parents, unmerged paths, and cleanliness; src/merger-role.ts checks only those fields. Targeted Merger Git/runtime tests pass (6/6) but contain no out-of-scope committed-path red.

Independent Git fixture verification demonstrated the semantic distinction: with conflict.txt conflicted, source-only.txt added only by the source parent, and unrelated.txt improperly edited during resolution, first-parent-to-merge listed all three paths, while automatic-merge-tree-to-merge and git show --remerge-diff listed only conflict.txt and unrelated.txt. Therefore the Review finding's root claim is sustained, but its literal phrase “any committed path outside the frozen scope” is too broad if implemented using a first-parent diff. The authorized repair is confined to resolution provenance at the existing Merger completion seam.
